lessons.title: Non-Fiction: What Is an Atlas?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about atlases from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about atlases.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a real atlas and discuss what it is.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about what atlases show and how they're used.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Look at an atlas or map app with your family.

lessons.title: Grid References (Simple)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use simple grid references to locate a position.
success_criteria: I can find a position using a letter and number.
I can describe a position using a grid reference.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using a simple grid (letters across, numbers down) to find and describe positions.
lessons.independent_task: Children find and record positions on a simple grid using references.

differentiation.greater_depth: Find and describe multiple grid references independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note introduction of grid references, linking maths and geography — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Play a simple grid reference game (like Battleships) with your family.

lessons.title: Using an Atlas
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use an atlas to find a country or feature.
success_criteria: I can find a country in an atlas.
I can use the index/contents.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap using a world map from earlier terms.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using an atlas to find a country, including using an index if age-appropriate.
lessons.independent_task: Children use atlases to find and record countries or features.
key_questions: Can you find this country in the atlas?
What does the atlas show about it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note atlas-using skill, a Year 2 geographical skills objective — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap what was found using atlases.
lessons.home_link: Look at an atlas or map app together.

lessons.title: Writing Map-Reading Instructions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write simple instructions for reading a map.
success_criteria: I can write instructions using sequencing words.
I can explain how to find something on a map.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing instructions for finding something on a map (e.g. 'First find the key, then look for the symbol').
lessons.independent_task: Children write 3-4 step instructions for reading a map.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note instructional writing applied to a geography skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share instructions with a partner and follow them.
lessons.home_link: Explain how to read a map to your family.

lessons.title: Grid References: Treasure Hunt
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply grid references in a practical activity.
success_criteria: I can follow a grid reference to find something.
I can give a grid reference for something I hide.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model a treasure-hunt style activity using grid references to find hidden items.
lessons.independent_task: Children play a grid reference treasure hunt game in pairs.
key_questions: What grid reference is this at?
Can you find what's hidden at B4?

differentiation.support: Adult supports grid reading during the game
differentiation.greater_depth: Create their own grid references for a partner to find

lessons.assessment_notes: Note practical application of grid references — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Create a simple grid reference game for your family.

lessons.title: Aerial Photographs: A Bird's Eye View
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to interpret features shown in an aerial photograph.
success_criteria: I can identify a feature from above.
I can compare it to a ground-level view.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the aerial view of the school from Week 2.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model interpreting a range of aerial photographs, identifying features from an unusual perspective.
lessons.independent_task: Children identify features in aerial photographs of different places, comparing to ground-level views.
key_questions: What can you see from above?
How is it different from ground level?

differentiation.greater_depth: Identify 5+ features and compare perspectives in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note aerial photograph interpretation skill, extended from Week 2 — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Look at a satellite/aerial view of your home area if possible.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Map Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read map-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read map words.
I can read a sentence about maps.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to map-themed words (e.g. 'grid', 'symbol', 'key').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading map words over the week.

lessons.title: Map-Themed Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a map/journey context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a journey/map context (e.g. distances travelled).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve map-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a journey word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Making Our Own Map Symbols
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to design symbols for a map key.
success_criteria: I can design a symbol.
I can explain what it represents.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model designing simple, clear symbols for common map features.
lessons.independent_task: Children design their own set of map symbols for a key.
key_questions: Is it clear what it means?

differentiation.greater_depth: Design 8+ symbols including less common features

lessons.assessment_notes: Note map-making skill: symbol design — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Design a symbol for something at home.

lessons.title: Giving Map Directions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to give clear directions using a map.
success_criteria: I can give a direction using the map.
I can use clear positional language.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model giving clear directions from one point to another using a map.
lessons.independent_task: Children give and follow directions using a simple map in pairs.
key_questions: How do you get from here to there?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and map skill combined — evidence for ENG.SL1/GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Give directions using a map or your knowledge of the local area.

lessons.title: Map Feature Data: Tally and Chart
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to record and represent data about map features.
success_criteria: I can record a tally of map features.
I can represent the data in a chart.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap tallying and charting from earlier terms.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model tallying features found on a map (e.g. number of houses, trees, roads), representing in a chart.
lessons.independent_task: Children tally and chart map features, answering questions about the data.
key_questions: Which feature appears most on the map?

differentiation.support: Adult supports tallying and chart construction

lessons.assessment_notes: Record data handling applied to a map context — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.home_link: Tally features on a map or in your local area.

lessons.title: Making Our Own Map with a Key
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a map including symbols and a key.
success_criteria: I can draw a map with symbols.
I can include a matching key.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a map using the designed symbols and a matching key.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own map of an imaginary or real place, including symbols and a key.
key_questions: Does your key match your map?

differentiation.greater_depth: Include 8+ features with a detailed key

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of map-making skills across the week — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Show your map to your family and explain the key.

lessons.title: Maps and Atlases Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about maps and atlases.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about maps and atlases, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why might a symbol be useful on a map?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on maps and atlases facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Grid References and Data
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply grid reference and data handling skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can use a grid reference.
I can read a data chart.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of grid references and data handling.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: grid references, data handling.
key_questions: What is at this grid reference?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 31 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.GEO/STAT.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising grid references over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maps, Atlases and Aerial Photographs Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key geographical skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can use a map, atlas or aerial photo.
I can explain what each is used for.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about geographical skills and resources.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Maps and Geography Skills' display combining maps, symbols, and aerial photo observations from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about maps and atlases?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's geographical skills learning — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished geography skills display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about maps and atlases with your family.
